item.title: The social media battlefield: Political campaigns in Bangladesh’s national elections
item.description: Bangladeshi political parties compete for Gen Z’s attention with viral content, while battling misinformation alongside street campaigning, as Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube become central arenas for political messaging and debate.

item.title: Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai receives a 20-year jail sentence
item.description: Jimmy Lai's sentence marks the harshest punishment among all prosecutions under the 2020 National Security Law, enacted by Beijing in Hong Kong.

item.title: Women and young girls bear the brunt of Mali’s worsening security crisis
item.description: Since 2012, Mali has been in security turmoil with the emergence and expansion of several radical non-State armed groups. This situation disproportionately affects the civilian population, especially women and girls.

item.title: Nepali poet Mani Lohani on life, literature, and the world of poetry
item.description: Sangita Swechcha of Global Voices interviewed Mani Lohani about his long career in writing and television journalism, his impact on Nepali poetry and fiction, and themes that shape his work.

item.title: War, bloodshed, and legitimacy: Is Iran witnessing another internal coup?
item.description: As war, succession anxieties, and public grief converge, debates resurface about how Iran’s system reshapes itself under extreme internal and external pressure

item.title: Is it useful to talk to a dictator? Belarusian opposition have doubts
item.description: Maria Kalesnikava made several calls to negotiate with the Belarusian dictator. This goes against the usual policies of both the Belarusian opposition in exile as well as the EU politicians

item.title: Burundi tea plantations hamper chimpanzee protection
item.description: In Burundi, tea production hampers the protection of endangered species, such as chimpanzees.

item.title: The paradox of Bangladesh’s democratic rebirth: A critical analysis of the 2026 election’s promise and pitfalls
item.description: With 127.7 million registered voters—including 64.8 million men, 62.9 million women, and 1,234 third-gender voters—the 13th National Parliamentary Election of Bangladesh represented one of the largest democratic exercises globally for 2026.

item.title: A rose by any other name? How one Trinidad Carnival band’s intimate gesture has sparked controversy
item.description: “You may dislike the choice [but] to declare that it denigrates culture is to flatten centuries of complexity into a single anxious conclusion.”

item.title: Women politicians face tech-facilitated violence in Uganda’s 2026 elections
item.description: Ideally, the law that is supposed to protect women online is the Computer Misuse Act 2011, but it has instead been used to attack feminist dissenters.
